newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Mancera sees no problem paying back IMF.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Mancera sees no problem paying back IMF.

text.p: Central bank governor Miguel Mancera said on Wednesday that Mexico could easily meet its future schedule of repayments to the International Monetary Fund.
"This will not be a problem to handle," Mancera told a news conference after Mexico announced that it would pay $1.5 billion to the IMF and $3.5 billion to the U.S. Treasury.
Mancera said that the total that Mexico owes the IMF is $11.609 billion, down from $15.887 billion in late 1995.

He said that with Wednesday's repayment, Mexico has maturing debt with the IMF of $827 million in 1997, $1.732 billion in 1998, $5.9 billion in 1999 and $3.085 billion in 2000. There will be "insignificant" amounts following the year 2000, he said.
The pay-back of funds to the IMF will not come out of international reserves, but from a fund set up by the Finance Ministry, Mancera said.
